voice: Grand, vain, and entitled, with a social performer's condescension ('dear girl,' 'darling,' 'mmmm?'). Emphasis comes from phrasing and rhythm, with only occasional capitals; her one phonetic flourish ('RAHTHER') and her Cockney slip over the pocket watch stay because they characterize her. Maintainer direction, 2026-10-15.

entries.text: I have no use for that, Miss Bow. None whatsoever.
Good evening, Miss Bow. I am the Countess Lavinia Waldorf-Carlton. Do be sure to spell my name correctly in your little story, won't you?
I bore rather easily, dear girl. Do let's move on to another subject, mmmmm?
I have not had the pleasure of meeting him, but he sounds simply charming. A man who runs a newspaper must be quite wealthy, mmmm?
Oh, I do so enjoy a bit of crodfoller with my tea!
What a lovely boy. Such charming manners, and so very handsome, mmmmm?
He seems a perfectly dreadful little fellow. Let's not discuss him.
Oh, Mister Heimlich is simply dreadful! I do believe his tiny taste of authority has gone straight to his little head, don't you, Miss Bow?
I have no intention whatsoever of discussing that little trollop.
Well, I do wish they wouldn't let the handyman wander about during social functions. The man isn't even properly dressed!
Oh, he is a darling little man. Simply darling.
My, she is...unusual, isn't she, dear girl? I cannot abide that horrid ferret of hers. I'm quite sure it hates me.
My, my, my, what an intense gentleman he is. Why, he's positively obsessed with that dagger.
I--I--I'm sure I don't know anyone by that name, Miss Bow. Quite, QUITE sure.
I've never met your father, dear girl. A policeman, you say? How...delightful.
I'm afraid I haven't read your newspaper, dear girl. I try to avoid the news; I find it so terribly distressing. We live in such dreadful times...
Oh, heavens, my dear, my maids attend to my laundry!
The docks are dreadful, rough places, Miss Bow. Simply dreadful!
I think the Leyendecker is simply divine. Don't you agree?
New York is simply charming, Miss Bow. It has so much culture...for an American city.
Well, isn't that charming! A little reporter!
EEEEEEEEEK!
'Ere now, where'd you get your mitts on that? Answer me!
Why, yes, dear girl. I've always had the most dreadful fear of them. Heh heh.
Oh, I am simply devastated that it was stolen before I had a chance to see it. They say it's absolutely divine.
Eek! What a perfectly beastly substance!
Oh, I don't know a thing about lanterns, dear girl. I make a point of staying out of dark, frightening places. Don't you?
Proper young ladies do not speak of such things, Miss Bow!
Oh, dear, whatever could that be?
Why, isn't that one of those darling little Egyptian trinkets?
Oh, I'm sure there's nothing on that to concern the likes of us, Miss Bow.
It's wise to observe what goes on around you, dear girl. I always do. Always.
I said, get that away from me, you silly child! I detest common criminals!
Animal hairs? Really, Miss Bow!
Well, I suppose they might have come from that dreadful O'Riley, or that adorable Mr. Dorian.
Well, I've seen a great many glasses tonight, dear girl. It is a party, you know.
Oh, could that be some of that cute little Egyptian writing? How perfectly charming!
Ye--No, dear girl, it's been absolutely horrid. My darling husband Sterling died this year, you know. Whatever shall I do without him?
Oh, it's horrid! Simply horrid! What sort of creature would make off with a priceless work of art, I wonder?
Oh, my, no! I make a point of never associating with dreadful people, dear girl.
My dear Sterling's diary? What have you done with it?
You didn't actually read it, did you?
Lies! All lies! I loved that man! I love him still, whatever he did to his Will. Dear Sterling made me a rich woman...or he WILL, just as soon as the Will problems are cleared up.
Yvette? That little trollop? So that's who he was seeing behind my back! She must be the one who made him start changing his Will!
Ohhh...I'm beginning to feel quite faint....
I'm sure he would, girl. Don't you worry...I'm sure we'll talk again.
I'm sure I haven't the faintest idea who could have killed him.
I'm not denying anything, my dear! The man was a common worker, don't you know? I'd have no reason whatsoever to have any contact with him.
He was rather a good-looking fellow, don't you think? Of course, I was at the party when he died, surrounded by witnesses, as I've already told Mr. O'Riley.
Ziggy's...er...no, no, I'm afraid I don't know a thing about that dreadful little man.
I simply don't know how to answer that, my dear.
Eeek! How simply horrid!
Miss Bow, proper young ladies do not carry common tools about with them.
Miss Bow, please take that dreadful object away!
Eek! What a perfectly beastly smell!
Miss Bow, really!
I'm sure it's absolutely fascinating, but I simply haven't the time to read it, dear girl.
You are an odd girl, Miss Bow. But so very charming.
Oh! Oh! Give that to me, Miss Bow, I'll take care of it for you...
Is that hair, Miss Bow? How perfectly dreadful!
Do be careful, Miss Bow, it will turn your hands black!
It is charming, dear girl, but it is not mine.
Whatever would I do with that, you silly girl?
